info.title: Inventory Control
info.description: Use Inventory Control to track your merchandise and maintain and analyze your inventory. This subscription is fully integrated with the other Sage Intacct subscriptions, particularly Purchasing and Order Entry.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Aisles
tags.description: An aisle is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find in the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Bins
tags.description: A bin identifies a specific location within a warehouse where items are or can be stored. Bins make it easier to find items during transaction processing.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Bin faces
tags.description: A bin face is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find within the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Bin sizes
tags.description: A bin size in an attribute you can assign to a bin to help determine whether the bin is suitable for storing certain items.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory cycles
tags.description: Create and use inventory cycles to keep track of when to take physical inventory.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Cycle counts
tags.description:
Cycle counting is an inventory auditing procedure in which a small amount of inventory is regularly counted in the warehouse. The general goal is to count the entire inventory over a period of time and update the inventory at the end of each count.

An inventory control cycle count object contains high-level information about a cycle count, such as the warehouse where the count is being conducted and the employee that will count the inventory. The lines in a cycle count represent individual items being counted.

For more information, see [Cycle counts overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Cycle_counts_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Cycle count lines
tags.description:
Cycle count lines represent the items included in a cycle count. You can create or update line items by modifying the cycle count.

A cycle count line records the quantity and location of an item included in a cycle count. Each line is associated with a specific cycle count through the `cycleCount` field.

For more information, see [Cycle counts overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Cycle_counts_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory documents
tags.description:
An Inventory Control document contains information about inventory transactions. An inventory transaction is usually an adjustment or a transfer. When you create a new document, it represents the first transaction in a workflow and it can only be converted to the next transaction in a workflow. 

For more information, see [Define transactions](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Create_Inventory_Transaction_Redirect) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document lines
tags.description: Line information for inventory transactions, including opening balances and adjustments. Create and maintain document lines from the owning [document object](inventory-control.document).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document line details
tags.description: This object contains warehouse inventory details for all or part of a document line, including serial number, aisle, bin, and row per item.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Document line supplies details
tags.description: This object provides inventory supplies details for document lines.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document histories
tags.description: An inventory document history contains one entry for each existing transaction in the workflow associated with the selected transaction.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory document subtotals
tags.description: Details of subtotals, taxes, discounts, charges, and more for an inventory transaction.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Supplies documents
tags.description:
A supplies document lists purchasing requisition line items that are enabled for the Supplies workbench. The Supplies workbench helps manage internal supplies that employees need day-to-day, and program-related supplies that support a company's mission or operations. 

For more information, see [Using the Supplies workbench](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=supplies-workbench) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Supplies document details
tags.description: This object provides supplies requisition details for line items listed in a supplies document.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Items
tags.description:
Items are goods, services, or kits that you purchase from vendors or sell to customers. Items are used in Inventory Control, Order Entry, and Purchasing. The type of an item (`itemType`) affects other item parameters. 
Possible item types are:
* `inventory` - Items that will be available in inventory, sales, and purchasing transactions.
* `nonInventory` - Items that will be available in both sales and purchasing transactions or contracts.
* `purchaseOnlyNonInventory` - Items that will only be available in purchasing transactions or contract expenses. 
* `salesOnlyNonInventory` - Items that will only be available in sales transactions or contracts.
* `kit` - The parent item of a (non-stockable) kit (which is assembled from other items at the time of the order). This type is only available if Kits is enabled in either Order Entry or Inventory Control.
* `stockableKit` - The parent item of a stockable kit (which is assembled from other items and stored before order). This type is only available if Stockable kits is enabled in Inventory Control.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item cross references
tags.description:
An item cross reference associates an inventory item with a specific customer or vendor, or with another inventory item.

When an inventory item is associated with a customer or vendor (known as an external cross-reference), the customer or vendor can provide their own identifiers for inventory items that can be used in transactions.

When an inventory item is associated with another inventory item (known as an internal cross-reference), you can provide an alternate item to substitute, upgrade, downgrade, or complement that item in Order Entry transactions in Sage Intacct. For more information, see [Item cross references](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Item_cross_references_OE) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item landed costs
tags.description:
A landed cost item is a non-inventory item that represents a landed cost expense, such as freight, insurance, customs duties, or handling fees.

This object is valid when Inventory Control is configured to enable landed costs.
For more information, see [Landed costs overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Landed_costs_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

Create and maintain landed costs from the owning [item object](inventory-control.item).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item vendors
tags.description: This object provides details about an item that can be purchased from a particular vendor. Create and maintain item vendors from the owning [item object](inventory-control.item).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse inventory information
tags.description: Warehouse inventory information is used with Inventory and Stockable Kit items. Sage Intacct uses the information from these records in the Inventory Reorders report.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse standard costs
tags.description: This object allows you to record different standard costs for different date ranges for item and warehouse combinations.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse vendors
tags.description: Use this object to specify the vendor information you want to use in the replenishment calculations for the item in this warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item groups
tags.description: An item group categorizes item dimension records, mainly for the purpose of structuring financial reporting.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item GL groups
tags.description: Item GL groups are used to organize transaction definitions for posting to the general ledger.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item warehouse available inventories
tags.description: This object provides information about available quantities for items, including warehouse tracking information.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item tax group item maps
tags.description:
An item tax group item map associates a tax schedule with items and item tax groups, which drive the taxes that are applied to a line item.

Applicable when using Advanced Tax without the Taxes module. For more information see [Tax Schedule Maps](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Taxes/Indirect_Tax/Sales_tax/Intacct_Advanced_Tax/Setup/advtax-tax-schedule-maps.htm).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Kit components
tags.description: Components are items included in a kit. Kits are common combinations of items that can be ordered and invoiced as a single item to simplify data entry. Kits can include inventory items, non-inventory items, and other kits.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Price lists
tags.description: A price list is a container for price list entries. Each associated price list entry should have a unique combination of item or product line, currency, start and end date range, and, optionally, minimum and maximum quantity range. For more information about price lists, see [Price lists - Order Entry](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Price_lists_oe) and [Price lists - Purchasing](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Purchasing_price_list) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Price list entries
tags.description: An inventory price list entry contains the pricing for a selected item within a selected price list. You can create price list entries for items whose prices are determined based on an amount, a discount or mark-up percentage, the quantity sold, and more.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Product lines
tags.description: Product lines are groups of related products. Using product lines makes it easier to update prices and track inventory movement. See [Product lines](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Order_Entry/Setting_up_Order_Entry/product-lines-OE.htm) for more information.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Rows
tags.description: A row is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find in the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Stockable kit documents
tags.description:
Component items in a stockable kit are assembled together to make it an inventoried item. Stockable kit documents provide a record of stockable kit build and disassembly transactions.

When stockable kits are built, the inventory of the components added to the stockable kit is reduced and the number of stockable kits is increased.
When stockable kits are disassembled, the inventory of the components removed from the stockable kit is increased and the number of stockable kits is decreased.

For more information, see [Kits](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_kits) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Stockable kit document lines
tags.description:
Each stockable kit document line object lists the stockable kits that were built or disassembled and the component items that were included in the kits. These transactions are recorded for inventory management and tracking purposes.

You can create or update document line items by creating or modifying the [stockable kit document](inventory-control.stockable-kit-document).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Posting summaries
tags.description:
An inventory control posting summary provides a summary of how an inventory transaction is posted to the general ledger (GL), including the resulting journal entry and related posting information.

**When to use**: Use the posting summary object to retrieve information about a transaction definition after it posts to the general ledger, including the journal entry record number. 

**Relationships**: Posting summaries are derived from inventory transaction definitions and are associated with the resulting general ledger entries generated during posting.

**Lifecycle context**: Posting summaries represent the final accounting outcome of the transaction and persist as part of the audit trail, supporting financial reporting, reconciliation, and traceability between operational inventory activity and financial records.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory totals
tags.description:
Use inventory totals to keep track of the items on hand that are available for sale. Sage Intacct is preconfigured with nine inventory totals for tracking inventory that's damaged, in transit, on hand, on hold, on order, requisitioned, or is scrap and spoilage. You can also create your own inventory totals as needed.

An inventory total can be assigned to a transaction definition so that the specified total is affected when a transaction with that definition template is saved. For more information and a detailed example, see [Inventory totals](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_Viewing_Inventory_Total_Information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Landed cost categories
tags.description:
Landed cost categories are labels that identify the distribution method for proportionately applying the amount of a landed cost, either estimated costs or actual costs, to the applicable inventory items in the original purchase transactions.

When you create a category, you can specify a distribution method of count, value, volume, or weight. For more information, see [Landed cost categories](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Landed_cost_categories) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Lot categories
tags.description: Lot categories let you group a specific set of items that have something in common. For example, you can create categories for items with similar characteristics, such as perishable goods, chemicals, medical supplies, or health and beauty products.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment forecasts
tags.description:
When the expected demand for an inventory item fluctuates greatly over time, for example if the item is seasonal, use a replenishment forecast to more accurately predict your inventory needs. During the replenishment process, Sage Intacct uses the replenishment forecast to determine the forecasted demand of the item during the vendor lead times to determine if the item needs reordering.

For more information see, [Replenishment](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=TOC_replenishment_setup) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment forecast lines
tags.description: Line items of the replenishment forecast. Each line item represents the forecasted demand for an item in a warehouse on a specific date. You can create or update line items by modifying the owning replenishment forecast.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment runs
tags.description:
This object contains details about purchase orders generated by an inventory replenishment run, including whether each requested purchase order was created successfully. 

A replenishment run record is generated each time you create purchase orders using the replenishment process to reorder items. For more information, see [Replenishment runs](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Replenishment_runs) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Replenishment run lines
tags.description: This line object represents the details of a purchase order generated from the owning replenishment run, such as the vendor, number of items, transaction amount, and creation state of the purchase order.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Serial masks
tags.description:
Serial masks define the format for product serial numbers. Serial numbers are strings of alphanumeric characters used to identify particular inventory items.

After creating a serial mask, you then assign the mask to appropriate inventory items. When users enter serial numbers for those items, the system checks that the numbers comply with the mask format. This helps ensure that serial numbers are consistent and valid across your inventory. 

For more information, see [Serial masks](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Adding_Editing_Viewing_Serial_Mask_Information) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Valuation maintenance objects
tags.description:
Inventory Control valuation maintenance operations allow you to detect any issues that may exist for your inventory valuation, including current unit costs and cost of goods sold (COGS), and update these costs.

Use the `action` property to specify whether you want to just analyze and report potential issues with your inventory valuation, or also update unit costs and COGS to resolve any issues detected. 

When you create a valuation maintenance object, you can choose to run it immediately or schedule it to run in the future. You can also specify filters to limit the scope of the operation, such as which warehouses, items, or cost methods to include. After the operation runs, you can view the results to see if any issues were detected and what actions were taken.

For more information, see [Schedule Inventory Valuation Maintenance](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Schedule_inventory_valuation_maintenance) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definitions
tags.description: A transaction definition includes the accounting rules, workflow settings, security settings, and other characteristics for a transaction. For more information, see [Transaction Definitions - Inventory Control](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Inventory_transaction_definitions) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition COGS GL details
tags.x-displayName: Inventory transaction definition COGS GL details
tags.description:
The inventory transaction definition COGS GL detail object defines the general ledger account mappings used when an inventory transaction posts cost of goods sold (COGS) adjustments. It ensures that inventory transactions consistently generate the correct debit and credit entries in the general ledger based on configured rules and dimensions.
**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve how inventory transactions map to COGS and related GL accounts, particularly for integrations that require accurate financial posting behavior. It is also used when configuring or validating accounting rules tied to inventory transaction definitions.





 **Relationships**: This object is part of inventory transaction definition configuration and works with related objects that define totals, subtotals, sources, and entity settings, collectively determining both the operational and accounting behavior of inventory transactions.

 **Lifecycle context**: This object plays a role in the posting stage of the lifecycle, where processed inventory transactions generate financial entries and update the general ledger with COGS and related account impacts.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition entity details
tags.description:
This object contains entity-specific configuration settings for an inventory transaction definition, including which entities can create transactions and how those transactions are configured at the entity level. These settings are applicable to transaction definitions that are configured to create transactions at the "Top level or entity" or "Entity only" level.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to determine or configure how a transaction definition behaves for specific entities, such as identifying where a definition is available, how transactions are numbered, or which templates are applied within each entity.

**Relationships**: Entity details are associated with an inventory transaction definition, which serves as the template governing the behavior of inventory transactions. They extend the base transaction definition by applying entity-level overrides and configurations in multi-entity companies.

**Lifecycle context**: Entity details are defined as part of transaction definition setup and configuration, particularly in environments using entity-level or top-level transaction creation. They are applied before transactions are created and remain in effect throughout the lifecycle of transactions generated under the definition, influencing document creation, numbering, and presentation at the entity level.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition sources
tags.description:
The inventory transaction definition source object defines how an inventory transaction can originate from other transaction types by specifying the document conversion rules and source relationships within a workflow. It ensures that transactions are created within the correct business context, with relevant data carried forward consistently and traceably.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve the valid source transactions for an inventory transaction definition, or when supporting document conversion workflows that rely on upstream transaction relationships.

**Relationships**: This object is part of Inventory transaction definition configuration and works with related objects that define entity behavior, totals, subtotals, and accounting impacts, collectively shaping how transactions are created, processed, and posted.

**Lifecycle context**: This object governs the conversion stage of the inventory transaction lifecycle, where upstream transactions are transformed into downstream transactions, ensuring that transitions between workflow stages follow defined and valid paths.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition subtotal details
tags.description:
Inventory transaction definition subtotal detail objects define the subtotal types supported by an inventory transaction definition and help structure how intermediate values are grouped within a transaction. Subtotal configuration shapes how transaction data is organized and presented as part of the overall transaction definition.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve the subtotal behavior for an inventory transaction definition, especially in integrations that depend on how transaction values are grouped before final totals are calculated. It is also relevant when you are documenting or validating transaction-definition configuration for inventory workflows.

**Relationships**: This object is part of Inventory configuration and works alongside related objects that define sources, totals, entity-level settings, and accounting behavior for the same transaction definition. Together, these objects describe how an inventory transaction is configured, processed, and tracked across the workflow.

**Lifecycle context**: This object plays its primary role during transaction-definition setup, where the structure and calculation behavior of inventory transactions are configured before users enter or process transactions. Its impact carries forward into transaction entry and processing by determining how subtotal information appears within the transaction's overall flow.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory transaction definition total details
tags.description:
The inventory transaction definition total detail object defines how an inventory transaction affects tracked inventory totals, such as on-hand or on-order quantities. It ensures that each transaction consistently updates inventory balances according to the rules configured in the transaction definition.

**When to use**: Use this object when you need to define or retrieve how a transaction impacts inventory totals or when building integrations that depend on accurate inventory balance updates.

**Relationships**: This object is part of Inventory configuration and works alongside related objects that define sources, subtotals, and accounting behavior to fully control how transactions are processed and recorded.

**Lifecycle context**: This object plays a role in the processing and posting stages of the lifecycle, where inventory transactions update balances and reflect their impact on stock availability and tracking.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Units of measure
tags.description:
Details for a unit of measure included in a unit of measure group. Sage Intacct places related units of measure into groups.
For example, the Count group includes related units of measure such as each, pair, and dozen. For more information, see [About unit of measure groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=About_uom_groups_oe).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Unit of measure groups
tags.description:
Unit of measure group are provided for items handled under Inventory Control, Order Entry, and Purchasing. Intacct places related units of measure into groups.
For example, the Count group includes related units of each, pair, and dozen. 
The unit of measure (UOM) groups that are provided with Sage Intacct cannot be deleted. Use the Sage Intacct UOM groups as is and create custom UOM groups. 
For more information, see [About unit of measure groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Order_Entry/Setting_up_Order_Entry/UOM_groups/about-UOM-groups-OE.htm).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouses
tags.description: A warehouse can be an actual warehouse, a store, or any type of stocking location or site that requires inventory tracking and management. Warehouse also serves as a dimension that can be set on transactions to expand report functionality and insight. See [Define warehouses](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Inventory_Control/Setting_up_Inventory_Control/Warehouses/warehouses.htm) for more information.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouse transfers
tags.description:
Use warehouse transfers to transfer items between warehouses or to transfer items between bins in the same warehouse. When you post a warehouse transfer, Sage Intacct creates the underlying system transactions, which includes automatically propagating the costs of the items.

You cannot change the cost of the items when they move into the destination warehouse. For more information, see [Warehouse transfers overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Warehouse_transfer_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouse transfer lines
tags.description: Lines in a warehouse transfer represent items included in the transfer and details about those items. You can create or update warehouse transfer lines by creating or modifying the [warehouse transfer](inventory-control.warehouse-transfer).

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Warehouse groups
tags.description:
A warehouse group categorizes warehouse dimension records, mainly for the purpose of structuring financial reporting.

For more information, see [About warehouse groups](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=IC-warehouse-dimension-groups) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Zones
tags.description: A zone is one of four optional attributes (zone, aisle, row, and bin face) you can assign to a bin to make it easier to find in the warehouse.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Item activity reports
tags.description:
An Item Activity report contains detailed information about which items are available (on-order, on-hand, and reserved quantity totals), and where they are located. Use the Item Activity report to view:
* Items available in each warehouse.
* Types of item transactions for a selected period.
* Availability of items that are components of a kit (creating a sales order for a kit moves the component items to reserved status).

For more information, see [Item Activity report](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Running_Item_Activity_Reports) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

tags.name: Inventory_Control_Inventory valuation reports
tags.description:
An Inventory Valuation report displays a list of inventory items, quantities available, item cost, and costing method. The total of all items is the total inventory value on the balance sheet.

The report is divided into two sections: Summary and Detail. The Details section shows what's on the shelf, the summary section shows the value in a warehouse.

For more information, see [Inventory Valuation report](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Running_Inventory_Valuation_Reports) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

objects.inventory-control.cycle-count.description: Cycle counting is an inventory auditing procedure in which a small amount of inventory is regularly counted in the warehouse. The general goal is to count the entire inventory over a period of time and update the inventory at the end of each count.

state.description:
Status of the cycle count. When a cycle count object is created, the initial state is set to `notStarted`. The state is then updated by the system as users work with cycle counts:
* `inProgress` - The items in the count are in the process of being counted.
* `counted` - The results of counting the items have been entered, and the count has been marked as complete.
* `reconciled` - The count results have been analyzed to evaluate the differences between the actual quantities that were counted and the system-recorded quantities, and Inventory Control transaction adjustments have been made for any count variances, if accepted.
* `voided` - The results of the count are not to be used, and the count has been marked as voided.

endDate.description: Specifies the date that the count was completed.

adjustmentDate.description: The date that automatically generated Inventory Control adjustment transactions were posted due to count variances during reconciliation.

quantityOnHandLastUpdateDate.description:
A read-only field that specifies the date and time when the quantity on hand was last updated. This field is refreshed when:
* A user clicks the Update quantity on hand button in the Sage Intacct UI
* Sage Intacct automatically updates the quantity on hand when a count is started

showQuantityOnHand.description: Specifies whether to continue to display the quantity on hand on the Cycle Count Information page after the count is started. This option cannot be changed after the count is saved.

excludedAllocatedQuantity.description:
Specifies whether the quantity on hand is reduced by the allocated (picked) quantity and, for tracked items, also by the reserved quantities in sales orders. 
Allocated quantity is considered to be picked and no longer on the warehouse shelves. 
Reserved quantity is considered to be on the warehouse shelves but set aside to fill sales orders and not available to be used anywhere else.

precision.description:
These numbers override the default precision, or number of decimal places, for this item in the Inventory Control, Order Entry, and Purchasing applications. 
For example, an item with a cost of $0.00456 requires five decimal places. Depending on your needs, you can assign the item a different precision in each application.
For example, you can enter 4 in Purchasing and Inventory and 2 in Sales. The default precision as shipped from Intacct is two decimal places for each application. However, for Order Entry and Purchasing, you can change this default to a precision of up to 10 decimal places in the application's configuration. 
While Sage Intacct uses the number of decimal places specified here for the item in transactions, it rounds values to 10 decimal places for costing calculations, to 2 decimal places for the General Ledger, and to 2 decimal places for reports. 
If your company is subscribed to Contracts, the value of Unit cost precision. Sales must either be blank or 10. In this scenario, the best practice is to leave this field blank.

The values you enter are used in the replenishment calculations and drive the reorder information displayed for the item on the Replenish Inventory.

Replenishment method for this item in the Vendor history. 
Provide how the amount to reorder is calculated.
Reorder point - base calculation on a specific reorder quantity and optional safety stock quantity Demand forecast by single value - base calculation on lead time for the vendor Demand forecast by statistical
account - base calculation on statistical journal entries for a statistical account (statistical account must be configured for inventory) See the information about replenishment methods and calculations in the Sage Intacct product help.

When the current net inventory falls to the reorder point plus the safety stock, the item is triggered for reorder. Use blank or positive integers. Applies when the replenishmentMethod is Reorder point

As an example, if 12 units are needed according to other replenishment calculations, a reorder quantity of 50 would cause the generated purchase order to be for 50. Applies when the replenishmentMethod is Reorder point

objects.inventory-control.replenishment-.description: This object provides information about the purchase orders generated from an inventory replenishment run. A replenishment run record is generated each time you create purchase orders using the replenishment process to reorder items.

key.description: System-assigned unique key for the replenishment run.

id.description: ID for the replenishment run. This value is the same as the key for this object.

href.description: URL endpoint for the replenishment run.

runDate.description: The date of the replenishment run.

runByUser.description: The ID of the user who created the purchase orders using the replenishment process.

key.description: Unique key for the user.

id.description: Login ID for the user.

href.description: URL endpoint for the user.

txnDefinition.description: The purchasing associated transaction definition for the purchase orders in the replenishment run.

key.description: Unique key for the transaction definition.

id.description: Name of the transaction definition.

href.description: URL endpoint for the transaction definition.

txnDate.description: The transaction date of the purchase orders in the replenishment run.

runState.description:
State of the replenishment run:
 * `success`- The system was able to create all of the purchase orders requested in the replenishment run.
 * `partialSuccess`- The system was able to create some of the purchase orders requested in the replenishment run but some failed. See the error message in the replenishment run lines for information about why the process failed.
 * `inQueue`- The replenishment run is waiting for the system scheduler to start the purchase order generation process.
 * `warnings`- The system was able to create all of the purchase orders requested in the replenishment run but there were warnings during the process. See the warning message in the replenishment run lines for information about the warnings.
 * `posted`- The purchase orders in the replenishment run have been posted.
 * `created`- The replenishment run has been created but the system has not started
 * `failed`- The system was not able to create any purchase orders requested in the replenishment run. See the error message in the replenishment run lines for information about why the process failed.

executionMode.description:
Execution mode of the replenishment run.
 * `online`- The replenishment run was created in the foreground. The system creates an online replenishment run when 10 or fewer purchase orders are to be created.
 * `offline`- The replenishment run was created in the background. The system creates an offline replenishment run when more than 10 purchase orders are to be created.

txnCount.description: The number of purchase orders in the replenishment run.

itemCount.description: The number of items requested to be reordered in the replenishment run.

purchaseAmountBase.description: The total purchase amount for all the items requested to be reordered in the replenishment run in the base currency.

txnAmountBase.description: The amount of the purchase order transaction in the base currency.

txnCurrency.description: Purchase order transaction currency with the vendor.

poCreateState.description:
State of the purchase order transaction creation.
 * created - The system successfully created the purchase order. All line items were processed and the transaction is ready for use.
 * warnings - The system created the purchase order, but there are warnings. See the `errorMessage` text for a description of the warnings.
 * failed - The system could not create the purchase order due to one or more errors, such as a closed GL period, an incompatible location or department, or a data validation failure. The transaction was rolled back and no purchase order exists in the system; see the error message for the specific reason.

errorMessage.description: If the `poCreateState` is 'failed', this error message explains why the purchase order wasn't created. If the `poCreateState` is 'warnings', this error message provides more information about the warnings encountered during the creation process.
errorMessage.example: The warehouse Location's currency has to be the same as document's currency in line 2; Base Currency has to be the same as Location's Base Currency in line 2; Error preparing values!; Could not create Document record!

objects.inventory-control.serial-mask.description: Serial masks define the format for product serial numbers. Serial numbers are strings of alphanumeric characters used to identify particular inventory items.

key.description: System-assigned unique key for the serial mask.

id.description:
ID for the serial mask. Specify one or more of the following characters:

* a - any lowercase alphabetic character
* A - any uppercase alphabetic character
* N - any number
* ? - any character
* space - space
* ' - quotation mark

Use quotes to define separators, such as hyphens or colons, or to define a fixed string of alphanumeric characters.

Any characters between quotes are handled as a fixed part of the sequence number. Two consecutive quotes represent a single quote.

length.description:
The number of characters in the serial mask. The number must match the total length of all the characters in the serial mask, including spaces.

For example, a serial mask of AANNN is 5 and of AA NNN is 6.

href.description: URL endpoint for the serial mask.

objects.inventory-control.valuation-main.description: Inventory Control valuation maintenance operations allow you to detect any issues that may exist for your inventory valuation, including current unit costs and cost of goods sold (COGS), and update these costs.

key.description: System-assigned unique key for the valuation maintenance object.

id.description: System-assigned ID for the valuation maintenance object. This value is the same as the key for this object.

href.description: URL endpoint for the valuation maintenance object.

summaryResults.description: Summary of the valuation maintenance operation and resulting cost changes.

name.description: User-specified name for this valuation maintenance object.

description.description: User-specified description for this valuation maintenance object.

state.description: Outcome of the valuation maintenance operation associated with this object.

emailAddress.description: Email address for receiving notifications related to this valuation maintenance object.

valuationFilters.description:
Filters that limit the scope of the associated valuation maintenance operation. The operation will be carried out for transactions whose entries include the items determined by applying the filters. 

When there are no transactions that include items that satisfy
the filter conditions (for example none in the specified item range belonging to the specified item group, or none identified by the specified item group, warehouse, and cost method combination), then
the valuation maintenance operation will still be recorded, but will take no action.

fromItem.description: The start of the item range for which to perform the valuation maintenance operation. If the `toItem` filter is not specified, then this filter identifies the only item for which to perform the valuation maintenance; otherwise, the valuation maintenance will be performed for all items in the range from `fromItem` to `toItem`, inclusive.

key.description: Unique key for the item.

id.description: Unique ID for the item.

href.description: URL endpoint for the item.

toItem.description: The end of the item range for which to perform the valuation maintenance operation. If the `fromItem` filter is not specified, then this filter identifies the only item for which to perform the valuation maintenance; otherwise, the valuation maintenance will be performed for all items in the range from `fromItem` to `toItem`, inclusive.

key.description: Unique key for the item.

id.description: Unique ID for the item.

href.description: URL endpoint for the item.

warehouse.description: The warehouse for which to perform the valuation maintenance operation. If this filter is not specified, then the valuation maintenance operation will be performed for all warehouses for items that satisfy the other specified filters.

key.description: Unique key for the warehouse.

id.description: Unique ID for the warehouse.

href.description: URL endpoint for the warehouse.

itemGroup.description: The item group for which to perform the valuation maintenance operation. If specified, then the valuation maintenance operation will be performed for all items in the specified warehouse (or in all warehouses if the warehouse filter is not specified) that belong to this item group. If this filter is not specified, then the valuation maintenance operation will be performed for all items in the specified warehouse (or in all warehouses if the warehouse filter is not specified) that satisfy the other specified filters, regardless of item group membership.

key.description: Unique key for the item group.

id.description: Unique ID for the item group.

href.description: URL endpoint for the item group.

costMethods.description: Cost methods to perform valuation maintenance; any or all of Average, Standard, FIFO, or LIFO

maintenanceSchedule.description: Schedule information for the associated maintenance valuation operation. If the `isScheduledOperation` property is false, then this schedule information will be ignored.

repeatPeriod.description: Repeat period or frequency of the schedule. For example, a repeat period of `weekly` with a repeat interval of `2` means the schedule will execute every 2 weeks. A repeat period of `monthly` with a repeat interval of `1` and a monthly repeat day of `dayOfTheWeek` means the schedule will execute on the same day of the week every month.

repeatInterval.description: Repeat interval (number of periods) between successive executions. For example, if `repeatPeriod` is `weekly`, a `repeatInterval` of `1` means the operation will run every 1 week; a `repeatInterval` of `2` means the operation will run every 2 weeks.

startDate.description: When to start the schedule. This date drives not only the start of the schedule but also the repeat by entries for daily, monthly, and yearly.

endDate.description: When to end the schedule, if the `repeatEndType` is set to `endOnDate`. This value will be ignored if the `repeatEndType` is not `endOnDate`.

monthlyRepeatDay.description:
For a monthly `repeatPeriod`, specifies the day of the month when the schedule executes:

* `dayOfTheMonth` - Use the day of the month from the `startDate` field. For example, if the start date is the 15th, then repeat on the 15th of subsequent months.
* `dayOfTheWeek` - Use the day and week of the month from the `startDate` field. For example, if the start day is a Monday, then repeat on the Monday after a month elapses.
* `endOfTheMonth` - Use the last day of each month.

This value will be ignored if the `repeatPeriod` is not set to `monthly`.

numberOfOccurrences.description: The number of times the schedule is executed when `occurrences` is specified for the `repeatEndType`. This value will be ignored if `repeatEndType` is not set to `occurrences`.

weeklyRepeatDay.description: For a weekly `repeatPeriod`, this specifies the day of the week when the schedule executes. This value will be ignored if the `repeatPeriod` is not set to `weekly`.

repeatEndType.description: Specifies whether the schedule ends, and if it should end on a specified date, or after a specified number of occurrences. If `never` is specified, then the schedule will have no end date; if `occurrences` is specified, then the schedule will end after the number of occurrences specified in the `numberOfOccurrences` field; if `endOnDate` is specified, then the schedule will end on the date specified in the `endDate` field. This value will be ignored if the `repeatPeriod` field is not specified.

isScheduledOperation.description: Specifies whether the associated valuation maintenance operation is a scheduled operation that executes according to the specified `maintenanceSchedule`.

maintenanceOptions.description: Specifies additional settings for the associated valuation maintenance operation.

asOfDate.description: The valuation maintenance operation considers only transactions on or after the specified date. This allows you to limit the scope of the valuation maintenance operation to transactions that have occurred since a certain date, for example since the last time you ran valuation maintenance.

action.description:
Specifies the valuation maintenance action: 
* `analyze` - Analyze costs only: Recalculates the inventory costs for transactions that occurred on or after the `asOfDate`. Identifies where the recalculated costs differ from the originally recorded costs, and generates reports with the results, without updating any costs.
* `update` - Analyze and update: Recalculates the inventory costs for transactions that occurred on or after the `asOfDate`, identifies where the recalculated costs differ from the originally recorded costs, updates the costs, and generates reports with the results.

transactionsToReport.description:
Specifies which transactions to report on: 
* `all` - Include all transactions.
* `costChanges` - Only transactions that have costing errors.

costUpdatePeriods.description:
Periods in which to update costs in the inventory subledger and internal cost tables.

When the `action` is `update`, this setting specifies whether the valuation maintenance operation is allowed to act on transactions in `closed` periods; otherwise it is ignored.

updateGL.description: Specifies whether to update the general ledger with recalculated COGS in open periods (occurring after the `asOfDate`) when the `action` is `update`. This setting is ignored when the `action` is `analyze`, since costs are not updated in that case, or for transactions in closed periods, since costs for those transactions will not be updated regardless of the value of this setting.

audit.description: Audit information for the valuation maintenance object.

objects.inventory-control.txn-definition.description: An inventory transaction definition includes the accounting rules, workflow settings, security settings, and other characteristics for a transaction.

key.description: System-assigned key for the transaction definition.

id.description: Unique name for the transaction definition. The name cannot be changed after the transaction definition is created.

href.description: URL endpoint for the transaction definition.

templateType.description: Specify the template type that is appropriate for the transactions that will be based on this transaction definition. Template type determines whether certain fields are included in a transaction.

description.description: A meaningful description of the transaction definition.

workflowCategory.description:
Workflow category for the transaction definition. Certain template types (`templateType`) should be associated with certain workflow categories as follows:
* `order` template type can be associated with these workflow categories: `receipt`, `transfer`, `shipping`
* `adjustment` template type can be associated with the `adjustment` workflow
* `list` template type can be associated with the `shipping` workflow
* `other` template type can be associated with the `adjustment` workflow

In the Sage Intacct user interface, the workflow category associates the transaction with the appropriate icon on the Overview page and with the applicable transaction menu grouping in the Inventory Control menu.

reportingCategory.description: Specify a reporting category that best reflects the purpose of the transaction definition so that similar documents can be grouped when building reports. (This field is applicable for use with Interactive Custom Report Writer or Interactive Visual Explorer subscriptions only.)

txnNumbering.description: Transaction numbering settings for the transaction definition.

enableSequenceNumbering.description: Set to `true` if you want to specify a numbering sequence for the transaction definition.

numberingSequence.description: If `enableSequenceNumbering` is set to `true`, specify the numbering sequence to use to automatically number transactions. Leave this field blank to number transactions manually.

key.description: Unique key for the numbering sequence.

id.description: Unique ID for the numbering sequence.

href.description: URL endpoint for the numbering sequence.

preserveSequenceNumbers.description: Set to `true` to ensure that numbers are never skipped. Enabling this option can affect performance when a large volume of transactions is entered at the same time.

inheritSourceDocumentNumber.description: Set to `true` if transactions should inherit source document numbers. If set to `true`, documents converted from this document will have the same document number.

inventoryControl.description: Inventory control fields apply only to companies subscribed to Inventory Control.

enableWarnOnLowQty.description: Set to `true` to alert users if the quantity needed is greater than the ONHAND total in the selected warehouse. The alert also shows the ONORDER and ONHOLD totals. In the Sage Intacct user interface, the alert displays when the user tabs out of the Quantity field in a transaction.

updatesInventory.description: The system assigns a value based on the inventory total details provided. If the inventory total details affect both quantity and value, this field is set to `quantityAndValue`.

updatesCost.description: The system assigns a value based on the inventory total details (`inventoryTotalDetail`) provided. This field is set to `true` if the transaction will update cost.

increaseOrDecreaseInventory.description: The system assigns a value based on the inventory total details provided and whether those totals are adding quantity/value or decreasing the quantity/value.

warehouseSelectionMethod.description: Determines how warehouses are presented to the user in the warehouse dropdown list in the transaction.

defaultWarehouse.description: Provide warehouse information only when the `warehouseSelectionMethod` is `useTheDefaultWarehouse`. Note that a user's default warehouse setting in their user preferences overrides this setting.

key.description: Unique key for the warehouse.

id.description: ID for the warehouse.

href.description: URL endpoint for the warehouse.

accounting.description: Accounting settings for the transaction definition.

txnPosting.description:
Specify whether the transaction post process creates a GL entry.  
`postToGeneralLedger`- The transaction posts directly to the General Ledger.
`doNotPost`- Transaction post process will not create a GL entry.

If you set to `postToGeneralLedger`, at least one debit and credit `inventoryAccountMapping` should be specified. A null value is processed as `doNotPost` for transaction definitions.

isSubTotalsEnabled.description: Set to `true` to allow users to specify standard subtotals for the transaction, such as tax or a discount. If this field is set to `true`, you must add at least one `subtotalDetail`.

conversionType.description:
Indicates how the system processes transactions that are partially completed.
`leaveTxnOpen` - converts the transaction to another transaction type, and the system leaves the original transaction open until the all items are completed.
`closeTxn` - converts the transaction to another transaction type, and the system closes the transaction regardless of whether the transaction is complete.
A null value is processed as `closeTxn`.

pricingAndTerms.description: Pricing and terms for the transaction definition.

initialPriceList.description: If layered price lists are in use, specify the first price list that the system will evaluate when determining a suggested transaction price.

key.description: Unique key for the price list.

id.description: ID for the price list.

href.description: URL endpoint for the price list.

specialPriceList.description: If layered price lists are in use, you can specify a special price list (for example, a discounted price list or seasonal price list). The special price list takes precedence over the `initialPriceList`.

key.description: Unique key for the price list.

id.description: ID for the price list.

href.description: URL endpoint for the price list.

print.description: Print settings for the transaction definition.

documentTemplate.description: Specify the printed document template to use for printed output (PDFs).

defaultText.description: If you do not provide a `documentTemplate`, specify any text that you want to appear on every document printed from this transaction.

enableUserOrGroupPermmission.description: This field has been deprecated. Use the `enableUserOrGroupPermission` field instead.

enableUserOrGroupPermission.description: By default, all users with the appropriate application permissions have access to transactions that use this transaction definition. To restrict access to certain users or groups, set this field to `true`.

userOverrides.description: User override settings for the transaction definition.

allowDepartmentOverride.description: Set to `true` to allow users to override the department set for the transaction.

allowLocationOverride.description: Set to `true` to allow users to override the location set for the transaction.

documentPermissions.description: Document permission settings. Settings that restrict editing, deletion, or require convert only, those settings only apply to posting. These settings do not impact a user's ability to save or edit draft transactions.

editPolicy.description:
Sets the edit permission for this transaction type.
* `noEdit` - The user cannot edit the transaction after it is created, unless it is in draft state.
* `beforePrinting` - The user can edit the transaction until it has been printed to PDF. After it has been printed, the transaction cannot be edited.
* `editInDraftOnly` - The user can edit the transaction until it has been posted. After it has been posted, the transaction cannot be edited.
* `all` - The user can edit the transaction as allowed by the transaction's condition. For editing restrictions, see [Edit a transaction](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Inventory_Control/Using_Inventory_Control/Transactions/inventory-txn-lists.htm?cshid=Inventory_txn_lists#Editatransaction) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

deletePolicy.description:
Sets the delete permission for this transaction type.
* `noDelete` - The user cannot delete the transaction after it is created.
* `beforePrinting` The user can delete the transaction until it has been printed to PDF. After it has been printed, the transaction cannot be deleted.
* `deleteInDraftOnly` - The user can delete the transaction only when it is in draft state. 
* `all` - The user can delete this transaction as allowed by the transaction's condition. For deletion restrictions, see (Delete a transaction](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Inventory_Control/Using_Inventory_Control/Transactions/inventory-txn-lists.htm?cshid=Inventory_txn_lists#Deleteatransaction) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

createPolicy.description:
Sets the create permissions for this transaction type.
* `newDocumentOrConvert` - The user can create the transaction as a standalone transaction or the user can create the transaction by converting the previous transaction in the workflow.
* `convertOnly` - The user can can only create this document by converting the previous transaction in the workflow.

multiEntityRuleForTxn.description: Sets the context for where users can create transactions from this transaction definition within a multi-entity, shared environment.

inventoryTotalDetail.description: Specifies the inventory running total that will be affected by resulting transactions and how the total will be affected.

subtotalDetail.description: Related inventory transaction subtotals. If `isSubTotalsEnabled` is set to `true`, you must add at least one subtotal detail.

inventoryAccountMapping.description: Related inventory transaction definition GL account mappings by item GL group. If `txnPosting` is set to `postToGeneralLedger`, enter applicable inventory account mappings. For example, if the transaction definition is for an adjustment that accounts for spoilage, you might debit the spoilage account and credit the Inventory account.

entitySettingDetail.description: Provides details about the entities that can create transactions, and also includes settings for each entity, such as numbering sequences and document templates. These details and settings are applicable to transaction definitions that are configured to create transactions at the `topLevelOrEntity` or `entityOnly` level.

objects.inventory-control.txn-definition.description:
Inventory account mapping details for inventory transaction definitions that post cost of goods (COGS) adjustments to the General Ledger.
For example, a transaction definition for a cost of goods adjustment related to spoilage can debit the spoilage account and credit the inventory account.

key.description: System-assigned unique key for the inventory transaction definition COGS GL detail.

id.description: Unique ID of the inventory transaction definition COGS GL detail. This value is the same as the `key` for this object.

href.description: URL endpoint for the inventory transaction definition COGS GL detail.

txnType.description: Specifies whether to debit or credit the corresponding GL account.

moduleType.description: Module type for this mapping. This value is always `inventory` because the COGS account is linked to an inventory transaction definition.

lineNumber.description:
Line number of the COGS GL detail on the inventory transaction definition.
If this value is not provided, the system automatically assigns a unique line number.
If a line number that is already in use is provided, the application adjusts other lines to keep line numbers unique.
When the transaction is posted, the system uses line numbers to post to the GL in the specified order.

id.description: ID of the GL account.

department.description: Default department for the line item. This value applies only when user override for department is not enabled. This setting is not applicable at the top level.

key.description: Unique key for the department.

id.description: ID of department.

href.description: URL endpoint for the department.

warehouse.description:
The item GL group and warehouse together define the account mapping criteria.
For example, you could have the Maintenance item GL group, Warehouse 13, and Hardware Customer GL group mapped to a COGS account
and Inventory account, and the Maintenance item GL group, Warehouse 13, and Software Customer GL group mapped to a different COGS account and Inventory account.

href.description: URL endpoint for the warehouse.

itemGLGroup.description:
The item GL group and warehouse together define the account mapping criteria.
For example, you could have the Maintenance item GL group, Warehouse 13, and Hardware Customer GL group mapped to a COGS account and Inventory account, and the Maintenance item GL group, Warehouse 13, and Software Customer GL group mapped to a different COGS account and Inventory account.

objects.inventory-control.txn-definition.description: Subtotal detail for an inventory transaction definition, including the supported subtotal type for the transaction definition.

key.description: System-assigned unique key for the inventory transaction definition subtotal detail.

id.description: Unique ID of the inventory transaction definition subtotal detail. This value is the same as the `key` for this object.

href.description: URL endpoint for the inventory transaction definition subtotal detail.

inventoryTxnDefinition.description: Inventory transaction definition associated with the subtotal detail.

key.description: Unique key for the inventory transaction definition.

id.description: ID of the inventory transaction definition.

href.description: URL for the inventory transaction definition.

lineNumber.description:
Line number for the subtotal on the inventory transaction definition.
If this value is not provided, the system automatically assigns a unique line number.
If a line number that is already in use is provided, the application adjusts other lines to keep line numbers unique.
The transaction definition uses line numbers to determine the display order of subtotals.

description.description: Description of the subtotal. A unique description is required to create an inventory transaction definition subtotal detail.

subtotalType.description: Type of subtotal to use for the inventory transaction definition subtotal detail.

appliedToLineNumber.description:
Subtotal line number to which the subtotal is applied.
Sage Intacct treats the initial subtotal line as line number 0.
The first defined subtotal in the transaction definition is line number 1, the second defined subtotal is line number 2, and so on.
If no value is provided, the applied-to line is assumed to be 0.
Taxes, other charges, and discounts are computed at the line level.
This field does not apply when line-level Simple Tax is used.

valueType.description: Value type used for the subtotal detail.

subtotalValue.description: Default value for the subtotal. If the value type is `amount`, enter the subtotal amount. If the value type is `percent`, enter the percentage as a whole number. For example, enter `10` for 10%. Users can override the default subtotal value in the transaction.

txnType.description: Specifies whether the subtotal will debit or credit the corresponding GL account and GL offset account.

glAccount.description: GL account to which the subtotal posts.

href.description: URL endpoint for the GL account.

id.description: ID of the GL account.

key.description: Unique key for the GL account.

offsetGlAccount.description: Offset GL account to which the subtotal posts. This field is only applicable when advanced workflows are used.

transferType.description:
Specify whether this is an immediate or in-transit transfer.
* An `immediate` transfer does not accommodate for the time it takes to move inventory from one warehouse to another. With an immediate transfer, ONHAND quantities are decreased at the source warehouse (the from warehouse) and increased at the destination warehouse (the to warehouse) at the same time.
* An `inTransit` transfer allows you to accommodate for the time it takes to move inventory between warehouses For example, warehouses may be across the city, across the country, or in different countries. While inventory is being moved, it's not in the ONHAND quantities at either the source warehouse (the from warehouse) or the destination warehouse (the to warehouse). Instead it's counted in the INTRANSIT quantity for the destination warehouse.
For more information, see [Warehouse transfers overview](https://www.intacct.com/ia/docs/en_US/help_action/Default.htm#cshid=Warehouse_transfer_overview) in the Sage Intacct Help Center.

action.description:
Sets the state that the transaction is in. If `transferType` is set to: 
* `immediate`, valid values are `draft` or `post`.
* `inTransit` and you are using a POST operation to create a warehouse transfer, valid values are `draft` or `transferOut`.
* `inTransit` and you are using a PATCH operation to update a warehouse transfer with a `transferState` of `draft`, valid values for the `action` field are `draft` or `transferOut`.
* `inTransit` and you are using a PATCH operation to update a warehouse transfer with a `transferState` of `inTransit`, the only valid value for the `action` field is `transferOut`.

Note that you cannot use the `action` field to change the `transferState` of a transfer that is `posted`, and you cannot set an `inTransit` transfer back to `draft`.
